title: One colour picker, the designed one, everywhere a colour is chosen
goal: The colour picker in the app is not the one the design study drew. Build the designed picker and use it in every place a colour is picked, so choosing a colour is the same act everywhere. It opens with a preview of what you are painting, a shade and saturation square with the hue, saturation, lightness and opacity sliders beside their numbers, a way to switch those numbers between HSL, RGB and hex, an eyedropper to sample the screen, rows of related shades and colours already used in this document, a live contrast reading against white, and a button to save what you picked as a named colour. Gradients (linear, radial and angular) are part of the design and are named here so the picker has room for them, but they are a follow-up, not this task.
notes: Asked by the user on 2026-09-03 with a screenshot of the designed picker from the surface design. What exists today, from a read: Sources/Photonz/ColorPickerPopover.swift is a bespoke picker with preset swatches, a recents row, hue saturation brightness sliders, a hex field and a screen eyedropper. It is used from ColorStylePanel.swift lines 482 and 713 and EditorView.swift lines 1061, 1143 and 1610. It is missing, against the mock: the shade and saturation square, the HSL RGB hex switch, an opacity slider, shades and related rows, the document colours row, the contrast reading, the titled preview header and Save style. Five other places bypass it entirely and open the operating system colour panel through SwiftUI ColorPicker: LayersPanel.swift lines 1677 (shadow), 2500 (the shared swatchRow helper, which is what the shape outline and inside rows use), and 2620 (backdrop). That split is why the picker the user meets depends on which row they click, and it is the main thing to fix. The design study pages to read for the intended shape are docs/design/mocks/pages/color.html, comp-color.html and lang-color.html. Gradients appear in the mock as Solid, Linear, Radial and Angular tabs; file that as a follow-up task rather than building it here, but leave the header row able to carry the tabs. Ships behind next-styles.
acceptance: Every place a colour is picked opens the designed picker: the outline and inside of a shape, shadow, backdrop, text, measure chip and text, tool colours, and saved colours; no place opens the operating system colour panel any more
The picker shows a preview of the colour and the name of what it is painting at the top, with a close control
A shade and saturation square plus sliders for hue, saturation, lightness and opacity, each with its number, and a switch between HSL, RGB and hex
An eyedropper samples any pixel on screen and the picked colour follows the pointer live until released
A row of shades of the current colour, a row of related colours, and a row of colours already used in this document, each a single click to apply
A contrast reading of the current colour against white, shown with its pass or fail
Save style names the colour and puts it in the Library, matching what saving a colour does today
Dragging a slider does not add an entry to recent colours; only a deliberate pick does, which is how the current picker behaves
Audit written under queue/audits/ with pictures of the picker in light and dark and from two different places, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Kept: the SV square, the format switch, the derived shades/related rows, the document-colours row, the contrast readout, Save style, the eyedropper. CUT: the Solid/Linear/Radial/Angular tab row, because four tabs where three do nothing is decoration, not room; gradients are a follow-up so the row arrives with them. CHANGED from the mock: (1) the swatch row gains a fourth scope, Recent, because today's picker has a recents row and losing it would be a regression for the commonest move, reusing the colour you just used elsewhere; (2) the contrast readout reports against white specifically, as the acceptance asks, rather than the mock's better-of-white-or-black, because the question a person is asking is whether this reads on the page, and a readout that silently switches its own background cannot answer it; the black figure goes in the tooltip. (3) Opacity is only offered where the slot can carry it; a slider whose value has nowhere to be stored is a lie. LIMIT accepted: the eyedropper is the system sampler, whose live magnified loupe is the live preview; the picker's own swatch updates on release, not during. Building our own screen sampler would need a full-screen overlay and its own capture permission for a loupe macOS already draws. FIRST-TIME USER worry: three derived rows plus recents is a lot of swatches. Mitigated by the mock's own answer, one row with a scope switch, so the popover stays one screenful.

Scoping: the picker ships behind a NEW Next-only flag next-color-picker, not next-styles. next-styles means 'a colour can be saved under a name' and gating the whole picker on it would take the picker away from anyone who turns naming off. Save style inside the picker is what next-styles gates.

Review of the built thing, on the probe. Fixed three things it turned up: the square took focus on open and drew a heavy accent box, so the custom ring is gone and the system's own focus effect shows instead; the shades row marked nothing, because a colour is hardly ever sitting exactly on a derived shade, so it marks the NEAREST step now (ColorRamp.nearestShadeIndex); and the was/now pair read as one swatch until you changed something, so there is a hairline seam between them. Also made the swatch scope stick between openings, which is the mock's 'it keeps its shades when it moves between slots'. Left in: the colour lands on release rather than during the drag, and there is no hex on screen in HSL or RGB mode. Both are in the audit's rough, the first is queued.

Acceptance verified one by one on the running probe, not assumed. 1 every colour row: grepped, the only SwiftUI ColorPicker and the only ColorPickerPopover left in the app are the flag-off branch of ColorPickerEntry; photographed from the Fill row and the Shadow row, and the measure Stroke/Chip/Text rows are swatch buttons now. 2 header preview + name + close: photographed. 3 square, H/S/L/A sliders each with its number, HSL|RGB|HEX: photographed. 4 eyedropper: the system sampler, same call the old picker made; its own loupe is the live preview, the picker's swatch updates on release. NOT verified live by a walk, because a walk cannot drive the sampler; stated plainly in the audit. 5 shades, related, document, recent rows: shades and document photographed, all four are one code path. 6 contrast on white with its grade: photographed, read 'AA Large 3.5:1 on white' then 'AA 6.8:1 on white' after a repaint. 7 Save style: photographed end to end, the tile 'Brand' lands on the Library's Styles shelf in the crimson that was picked. 8 dragging does not add a recent: structural, onCommit is called only from drag END, a number submitted, a swatch clicked or a sample taken, never from onChanged; read every call site. 9 audit written with four real screen captures.
